agents.name: Bob
memories: Water is the constraint that ends farms.
Do not plant more than we can water.

today.why: The stalks are ripe now. Leaving ripe corn on the stalk is how a careful farm turns into a hungry one — get it in the bin before weather or pests write a different ending.
today.expect: Corn in storage, field clear, food buffer thick enough for the next stretch.

yesterday.why: Stalks just pushed into growing under clear sky. Water is the constraint that ends farms — three points a day still drip even with the ditch, and I will not let a thickening row go thirsty on my watch.
yesterday.expect: East field moisture held high so growing can push toward ripe without a dry spell.

agents.name: Alice
memories: Unused seeds are a delay, not a reserve.
Ditches compound. Heat does not wait.

today.why: Unused seeds are a delay, not a reserve. The moment the row clears, put the next one in — heat does not wait for a tidy schedule.
today.expect: A seeded row again so we do not sit on an empty field while the cistern and ditch already work.

yesterday.why: Corn is thickening on its own now. Unused timber is a delay too — a woodpile before we need fence or fuel beats empty hands when the next idea needs boards.
yesterday.expect: Wood stock up while the crop cooks, without burning another morning on the same cistern loop.
